judgment_text:
Prayer in W.P. No. 21317/2022: To direct the respondents to forthwith hand over possession of the land measuring 800 sq. mtrs. comprised in Survey No. 269/4B, Maduravoyal Village and Taluk, Chennai District, Previously Tiruvallore District, allotted to the petitioner in terms of G.O. Ms. 251/Rev. Department dated 24-3-1994, after removing the encroachments in pursuance of and consequent upon the 4th respondent The Tahsildhar, Maduravoyal, letter ref. no. Na.Ka. 10079/1994/A1, dated 10-7-2018, calling upon the Inspector of Police, T4-Maduravoyal Police Station, to provide police Station, to provide police protection for removal of encroachments

Prayer in W.P. No. 18278 of 2015: To direct the respondents to consider the petitioner Application for Regularization dated 11-2-2008

The Order of the Court was delivered by

S.M. Subramaniam, J.:— Writ Petition in W.P. No. 21317 of 2022 has been instituted to direct the respondents to forthwith hand over possession of the land measuring 800 sq. mtrs. comprised in S. No. 269/4B, Maduravoyal Village and Taluk, Chennai District, previously Tiruvallore District allotted to the petitioner in terms of G.O. Ms. 251/Rev. Department dated 24-3-1994 after removing the encroachments in pursuance of and consequent upon the 4th respondent/The Tahsildhar, Maduravoyal Letter ref. no. Na.Ka. 10079/1994/A1 dated 10-7-2018, calling upon the Inspector of Police T4-Maduravoyal Police Station to provide police Station to provide police protection for removal of encroachments.

2. The petitioner is Help Age India, a registered Society. The Government, based on the request of the petitioner issued G.O. Ms. 251/Rev. Department dated 24-3-1994 allotted a land at Maduravoyal Village. The proposal for allotment of land was considered by the Government under Section 24 of the Tamil Nadu Urban Land (Ceiling and regulation) Act, 1970 (in short “the Act, 1970”) and accordingly allotted the land measuring 800 sq. mtrs. in S. No. 269/4B in favour of the petitioner. Land was allotted, subject to the following conditions:

“(i) The helpage India/state Federation of the Deaf shall pay the cost of acquisition plus 50% service charges as land value, and for the value of trees, wells and structures if any.

(ii) The Helpage India/State Federation of the Deaf should utilise the land for the purpose specified within a period of one year from the date of taking possession of the land. The land shall not be utilised for any other purpose except the purpose specified in para 4 above.

(iii) The lands allotted shall not be transferred by way of sale, gift, mortgage, lease or otherwise to any person or institution.

(iv) The land value shall be paid within 30 days from the date of receipt of orders fixing the land value.

(v) If the Helpage India/State Federation of the Deaf Madras fails to remit the amount within a period of thirty days, the allotment is liable to be cancelled, without assigning any reason.

(vi) The possession of the lands shall be handed over by the Collector of Chengalpattu M.G.R. to the Helpage India/State Federation of the Deaf on remittance of value of land.

(vii) In the event of the Helpage India/State Federation of the Deaf not complying with any other conditions of allotment, the Government shall, after giving an opportunity to them to be heard in the matter, cancel the allotment and the lands shall revest to the Government free from all encumbrances. No compensation shall be payable in respect of any building or other supersturcture constructed on such lands, revesting to the Government under this clause.

5. The land value shall be credited to “0029 - Land Revenue - 00. Land Revenue - 800 - Other Receipts - AO Receipts under the Tamil Nadu Urban Land (Ceiling and regulation) Act, 1978 (D.P. Code No. 002900300AO0007)”.

3. The petitioner would submit that possession has not been handed over to them and encroachers occupied a portion of the land allotted to the petitioner. Thus, the petitioner submitted an application for removal of encroachment. Though enforcement actions were initiated under the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905, till date possession has not been handed over to the petitioner. Thus, the present writ petition has been instituted.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that once land is allotted, it is the duty cast upon Authorities to ensure that the land is free from encroachment and on account of encroachment, the land is unable to be utilized by the petitioner.

5. The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for R 1 to R 4 would oppose, by stating that lands were allotted at the request of the petitioner for the purpose of establishing a Mobile Medicare Unit, Training-cum-Research and Development Centre, Day care centre, consulting unit, etc. by the petitioner. Lands are not utilized for the purpose for which it was allotted by the Government in the year 1994. 32 years elapsed and till now, lands have not been utilized as per the conditions annexed along with the Government Order. Therefore, the Government is empowered to cancel the allotment and utilize the land for public purpose.

6. This Court is of the considered view that lands were allotted “as is where is condition” and if at all any grievance existed during the relevant point of time, when the land was allotted, petitioner could have resolved the same,. Admittedly, original owners of the land, after issuance of notification under the Act, 1970, had executed sale deeds in favour of few persons and they are in occupation of the land. Therefore, rights of those subsequent bona fide purchasers are also to be adjudicated. Any subsequent sale effected, after issuance of notification under Section 6 is void. However, the disputes are to be resolved in the manner known to law. The fact remains that those subsequent purchasers are in occupation of the land. It is for the Government to initiate action for eviction of unauthorized occupants and encroachments as the case may be, if any decision is taken to cancel the allotment made in favour of the petitioner.

7. As far as the petitioner is concerned, lands were allotted in the year 1994 and for the past 32 years, possession has not been taken nor lands are utilized for the purpose for which it was allotted by the Government. Now, Maduravoyal is part of Chennai Corporation and on account of skyrocketing of market value in the particular locality, these litigations are continuing in one way or the other, which need not be encouraged by the Court. Complex situations arose on account of multiple transactions occurred between the parties after issuance of notification under the Act, 1970 are to be adjudicated in the manner known to law.

8. As far as the claim of the Government is concerned, they are empowered to invoke the conditions stipulated in G.O. Ms. 251/Rev. Department dated 24-3-1994 for cancellation of allotment and to deal with the subsequent sale executed after issuance of notification under the Act, 1970. Leaving open all these issues to be resolved between the parties, W.P. No. 21317 of 2022 stands disposed.

9. In view of the order passed in W.P. No. 21317 of 2022, no further adjudication is required in respect of Writ Petition in W.P. No. 18278 of 2015. Accordingly, the said W.P. No. 18278 of 2015 is closed. No costs.
